title: Cobalt Insurance POC assurance matrix and artifacts
content:
Summary:
This document is the working assurance matrix and artifact index assembled for the Cobalt Insurance POC (Nov–Dec 2025). It maps the customer questionnaire and workshop concerns to concrete evidence artifacts, short-form answers suitable for submission, and an action list for follow-up items. The goal is to provide Cobalt a reproducible bundle for their internal audit team and to track outstanding evidence requests that require engineering or compliance work.

Scope and context:
- Customer: Cobalt Insurance (data residency: us-east-1; regulated financial workloads).
- Deployment model proposed for POC: Redwood Dedicated (single-tenant GPU pool) with optional VPC peering for secure egress to Cobalt systems.
- Controls baseline: SOC 2 controls implemented; ISO 27001 in progress; supplementary controls documented here for the POC.

How to use this doc:
- Reference the "Question -> Short Answer -> Evidence" rows when filling the customer's questionnaire.
- Artifact filenames reference S3 or Drive locations in linked_artifacts or the artifact index below.
- Action items at the end show owners and target dates.

Assurance matrix (selected questions from Cobalt questionnaire):
1) Q: Do you support customer-managed encryption keys for model and request data at rest?
   Short answer: Yes — Redwood Dedicated supports customer-managed keys (CMKs) via AWS KMS. Key material can be restricted via IAM and key policies; we can also integrate with vendor HSMs in Private deployments upon contract.
   Evidence: s3://redwood-evidence/cobalt-insurance/2025-11-20/kms-architecture-diagram.png; drive://shared_drives/security-and-compliance/km-policy-snippets.txt
   Notes: For the POC we'll enable a customer-owned KMS alias and provide a key policy template. Engineering task: confirm tenant key rotation schedule with infra (SEC-4332).

2) Q: How is customer traffic isolated from other tenants?
   Short answer: POC will use Dedicated pools with network-level isolation and VPC peering; traffic for inference stays on our dedicated NICs and does not traverse shared overlay networks.
   Evidence: s3://redwood-evidence/cobalt-insurance/2025-11-20/network-segmentation-diagram.pdf; github PR infra#987 (dedicated-pool-aws-cfn).
   Notes: Provide live diagram and BGP/assertion logs during workshop demo.

3) Q: Do you retain logs that could contain customer PII? What is retention and access control?
   Short answer: Access and request logs are retained for 90 days by default for Dedicated; retention configurable by the customer. Sensitive fields can be redacted at ingress. RBAC restricts access; all log access is audited.
   Evidence: drive://shared_drives/security-and-compliance/log-retention-policy-2025.md; s3://redwood-evidence/cobalt-insurance/2025-11-21/audit-log-sample.json (redacted).
   Notes: Cobalt requested 365d retention for compliance; product team needs to validate impact on storage and cost (ticket ENG-7654).

4) Q: Describe pentest results and remediation cadence for the service.
   Short answer: We perform annual third-party penetration tests and quarterly internal scans; remediation windows tracked in our vulnerability tracker. The latest third-party report (Oct 2025) has no critical findings.
   Evidence: drive://shared_drives/security-and-compliance/cobalt-insurance-pentest-report-2025.pdf; https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-4148 (vuln remediation board).
   Notes: Cobalt asked for a delta report for the POC timeframe — SOC will prepare an executive summary by 2025-12-07.

5) Q: Can you demonstrate separation of customer data in memory/kv cache during inference?
   Short answer: Yes — runtime enforces model execution contexts with per-tenant KV namespaces and zero-copy isolation. KV caches are namespaced and flushed on instance tear-down for Dedicated.
   Evidence: s3://redwood-evidence/cobalt-insurance/2025-11-19/kv-cache-flush-test.log; github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/commit/8b3f2a4 (namespace-enforcement).
   Notes: We performed a flush-and-verify test in the POC lab; logs attached.

Artifact index (files prepared for Cobalt):
- kms-architecture-diagram.png — diagram of KMS integration and key ownership flow (s3 path above).
- network-segmentation-diagram.pdf — Dedicated pool + VPC peering routing map.
- log-retention-policy-2025.md — policy excerpt showing default retention, redaction options, and audit controls.
- cobalt-insurance-pentest-report-2025.pdf — third-party pentest exec summary (redacted for non-disclosure).
- kv-cache-flush-test.log — automated run showing flush and verification steps (redacted).
- vpn-config-export.json — exported VPN parameters used for test peering (linked_artifacts).
- access-roles-and-policies.txt — minimal IAM roles we propose for Cobalt operator accounts.
- onboarding-runbook.md — step-by-step runbook used during the workshop to stand up a Dedicated pool and perform smoke tests.

Sample canned responses (for questionnaire submission):
- Data residency: "Customer data for the Dedicated pool resides in the customer's selected region (us-east-1 for the POC). We support region locking and do not replicate data to other regions without explicit configuration."
- Third-party audits: "Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II program; the SOC 2 report is available under NDA. We perform annual external penetration tests and quarterly internal scans."
- Privileged access: "Administration access is role-based and multifactor authenticated. All privileged activity is logged and subject to periodic review; emergency access requires an approval workflow recorded in the audit trail."

Workshop notes (Nov 19, 2025 demo + breakout):
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood Infra), Priya Nair (Security), Cobalt technical leads: A. Patel, J. Nguyen; compliance: S. Faulkner.
- Demo: VPC peering setup, CMK key ownership walk-through, and a KV flush demonstration.
- Raised issues: Cobalt compliance asked for signed artifact manifest and hash checksums for evidence files; they also asked for sample compliance language to insert into their vendor inventory.
- Follow-ups agreed in meeting: see Action items below.

Action items and owners:
- (SEC-4332) Provide key policy template and confirm rotation schedule — Owner: Priya Nair — Due: 2025-12-02
- (ENG-7654) Validate 365d log retention cost and provisioning for Dedicated pools — Owner: Liam O'Connor — Due: 2025-12-09
- (SEC-4345) Produce pentest delta executive summary for the POC window — Owner: Rachel Summers — Due: 2025-12-07
- (SRE-1122) Export artifact manifest with SHA256 checksums for all evidence files and place in s3://redwood-evidence/cobalt-insurance/manifest.json — Owner: Diego Alvarez — Due: 2025-12-04
- (SE-2033) Draft vendor inventory blurb and suggested contractual language for Cobalt security team — Owner: Maya Chen — Due: 2025-12-03

Risks and mitigation notes:
- Risk: Log retention extension increases cost and may require storage lifecycle automation. Mitigation: Offer tiered retention with archive to Glacier-equivalent after 90 days. Action: ENG-7654.
- Risk: Customer requires HSM-backed key material for their Q3 audit. Mitigation: Private deployment + HSM integration is supported; need commercial discussion and timeline.

Next steps for distribution:
- Circulate this draft to the Cobalt technical and compliance contacts with the redacted artifact bundle (link to Drive).
- On approval, produce a signed evidence manifest and a short readout deck (2 slides) summarizing controls and artifacts for executive reviewers.

Appendix: short file checks and notes for reviewers:
- All PDF/scan artifacts have been redacted for PII before upload. Confirm redaction logs in S3 (see manifest task).
- Avoid sharing full pentest report to non-NDA stakeholders; use the provided exec summary.
- For any additional evidence requests (e.g., SIEM correlation rules), open a new ticket and reference SEC-4332 in the subject.
